brief: Deutsche Bank's weekly positioning monitor extends its prior argument that equities are range-bound between earnings seasons. The S&P 500 chopped in a tight range of just over 2% over the last month despite Jackson Hole, geopolitical and trade escalation, CPI and payrolls, and positioning moved sideways with it, overweight but not elevated at the 65th percentile and well below levels implied by earnings growth. The aggregate 0.34sd splits into discretionary investors at neutral (47th percentile) and systematic strategies overweight at 0.76sd (85th percentile). Vol control allocations sit at the 100th percentile, so funds have limited capacity to add while downside flows could accelerate in larger drawdowns, though sensitivity to sell-offs fell this week. CTA equity exposure at the 83rd percentile now depends more on declining volatility than on stronger trend signals. Across sectors only MCG and Tech and Energy are overweight. Equity fund inflows slowed to $2.8bn, the lowest in two months, as broad-global, Japan and Europe inflows were offset by US, China and Taiwan outflows, while bond and money market inflows stayed healthy.
